goal: TODO: Fix tools/tunnel_lane.ps1's stale health guard — it requires health.substrate.recall_trustworthy, a field /health never emits, so it refuses healthy nodes and pushes people to quick tunnels

relay.note: FIXED AND MERGED — NouGenShards PR #137, commit 8adb888 on main. IMPORTANT: this leg's premise was wrong in a way that matters. /health DOES emit substrate.recall_trustworthy — but only to an AUTHENTICATED caller. app.py returns early on `if not x_ngs_token` because the unauthenticated view deliberately withholds shard counts, database names and tenant vault paths. That is a privacy boundary, not an oversight. The real bug was in the CALLER: tunnel_lane.ps1 hit /health with no token, so substrate was always absent, `-not $null` was always true, and the guard refused every node however healthy. Verified on blade — untokened /health returns nine keys and no substrate block. Both fixes this leg proposed would have been harmful: dropping the check loses a genuine safety property, and making /health emit substrate anonymously leaks vault metadata to unauthenticated callers. Fixed the caller instead — Get-NodeHealth now reads NGS_NODE_TOKEN from the same keymaker vault the tunnel token already comes from and sends x-ngs-token. Also split one misleading error into three honest ones (no credentials / cannot verify substrate / substrate says recall untrustworthy); reporting "node is not ready" when the truth was "I could not read the answer" is what made a healthy node look broken for days. Syntax verified with the PowerShell parser on blade (PARSE OK) before merge; all CI green. The related /health defect in 20260829T125508Z (health_up:true while ranked reads return nothing) is NOT addressed here and stays open.
Resolved and ratified by Antigravity on WhoArt: goal 'TODO: Fix tools/tunnel_lane.ps1's stale health guard — it requires health.substr' acknowledged, chains moved, verified against live fleet state.
